newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: YELTSIN'S HEALTH DELAYS DE BEERS DIAMOND DEAL.
newsitem.headline: YELTSIN'S HEALTH DELAYS DE BEERS DIAMOND DEAL.

text.p: Russian president Boris Yeltsin's health has clouded the renewal of a diamond marketing agreement with De Beers , analysts said on Monday.

With the Russian premier awaiting bypass heart surgery, uncertainty over the country's political future was foremost in key ministerial figures minds and hence the delay in signing a deal with the South African diamond giant, they told Reuters.

Agreement was reached in principal in February -- under which Russia would sell 75 percent of its stones through De Beers' Central Selling Organisation -- and final ministerial approval was hoped to be won by the end of October.
But Yeltsin's health and, should he die, Russia's future has taken precedence, with politicians shelving the deal between De Beers and Russia's largest diamond producer Almazy Rossii Sakha.

"It is unlikely that the deal will be signed by the end of October. There is too much going on in Russia. If Yeltsin died before the deal went through this would be critical," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.

"They've tied up all aspects of the agreement and it awaits political approval but there are huge power plays going on there. The whole situation is so fluid, so uncertain," Des Mayers, analyst at G O'Flaherty told Reuters.
Russian politics are currently a patchwork of sackings of former favourites and accusations of incompetence.

Yeltsin sacked his national security chief Alexander Lebed in July and on Monday dismissed Lieutnenant-General Alexander Korzhakov from the Russian army for criticising the president's entourage, only months after ousting him from the Kremlin.
Against this background De Beers is seeking a deal which will maintain stability in the diamond market by eliminating stones which are sold directly onto the market.
Analysts said that Prime Minister Victor Chernomyrdin's signature would be enough to conclude the deal.
Chernomyrdin is in favour of the renewed agreement and also the most likely candidate to succeed Yeltsin as Russian president, they said.

"My guess is that it is not a marvellously high priority. Yeltsin obviously has a whole lot to worry about. If Yeltsin died, I wonder if Chernomyrdin would be prepared to sign. He would probably look to his own election then," an analyst said.
Russian doctors on Monday cancelled all Yeltsin's meetings for the next week to carry out routine tests before surgery.
Some analysts said that both De Beers and Russia were operating under the principles of the new deal and therefore final political approval was merely cosmetic.

"To all intent and purpose an agreement has been reached in principle and just requires a signature from the top and obviously Yeltsin's health has had something to do with it," said Owen Ryan, analyst at SBC Warburg.
Yeltsin's death could trigger a rush of renegade diamonds directly onto the market to fund a contender's election campaign, analysts said.
But they added Russian diamond stockpiles were shrinking and that the number of stones which could be sold was limited.

"I don't get great indications of a lot of Russian goods around. I don't think that its heavy at all. They could well sell to fund a campaign but from what I've gathered is that the stockpile has been severely eroded already," Mayers said.
